title: Which token should I use for muted text?
summary: Use --color-text-muted (#64748b) on white: 4.76:1 measured. On pale indigo it fails; use --color-text-secondary.
short: Use `--color-text-muted` (#64748b){ref:ds-tokens} for muted text on white. It measures 4.76:1 against `--color-surface` (#ffffff){ref:measured}, above the 4.5:1 that WCAG requires for normal text{ref:sc143}. On the pale indigo `--color-primary-surface` it measures 4.26:1 and falls below that minimum{ref:measured}, so use `--color-text-secondary` there.

sections.heading: Measured contrast of the six text roles
body: The six text roles are neutral slate tokens{ref:ds-tokens}. The table gives each one measured against white (`--color-surface`). The last column states whether the ratio reaches the 4.5:1 minimum for normal text{ref:sc143}. The DS presents the first five as one neutral-hue text scale and `--color-text-disabled` as state only{ref:ds-colors}.

sections.heading: Where muted text stops working
body: Muted text clears the minimum on white and on the light gray surface, with a thin margin on the gray. It does not clear it on the indigo tint.{ref:measured}{ref:sc143}

sections.heading: The DS floor for muted text
body: Rule: muted text is never lighter than #64748b (slate 500) on white{ref:ds-agents}. Why: lighter slate values fall below 4.5:1; slate 400 (#94a3b8) measures 2.56:1 on white{ref:measured}, below the 4.5:1 minimum{ref:sc143}.

sections.heading: Copyable CSS
body: Import the tokens once at the app entry, then reference the role token. Never hardcode the hex{ref:ds-agents}.

faq.q: Which token should I use for muted text on a white background?
faq.a: Use `--color-text-muted` (#64748b){ref:ds-tokens}. It measures 4.76:1 on white{ref:measured}, above the 4.5:1 minimum for normal text{ref:sc143}.

faq.q: Can I use a lighter gray for muted text?
faq.a: Not on white under the DS rule: muted text is never lighter than #64748b{ref:ds-agents}. Slate 400 (#94a3b8) measures 2.56:1 on white{ref:measured}, below 4.5:1{ref:sc143}.

faq.q: What should I use for muted text on an indigo tinted background?
faq.a: Use `--color-text-secondary` (#475569). `--color-text-muted` measures 4.26:1 on `--color-primary-surface` (#eef2ff), below 4.5:1, while secondary text measures 6.78:1 there{ref:measured}.

faq.q: Is --color-text-disabled a good choice for less important text?
faq.a: No. It measures 1.48:1 on white{ref:measured} and the DS reserves it for the disabled state, not readable text{ref:ds-colors}.

faq.q: Does muted text pass on the light gray surface?
faq.a: Yes, with a thin margin: 4.55:1 on `--color-surface-secondary` (#f8fafc){ref:measured}, against a 4.5:1 minimum{ref:sc143}.

faq.q: Should I hardcode the muted gray value?
faq.a: No. Reference `var(--color-text-muted)` after importing `@ramoslabs/tokens/css` once; a raw hex in CSS is a defect under the DS rules{ref:ds-agents}.
